hints: Take natural logarithms of both sides of $a^{2y - 1} = b^{x - y}$.
Expand brackets and group all terms involving $y$ on one side and terms involving $x$ on the other side.
Explain why the resulting relation matches the standard straight-line form $y = mx + c$.
walkthrough:
Take the natural logarithm of both sides of $a^{2y - 1} = b^{x - y}$:
$$\ln\left(a^{2y - 1}\right) = \ln\left(b^{x - y}\right)$$

Apply power laws of logarithms $\ln(u^v) = v\ln u$:
$$(2y - 1)\ln a = (x - y)\ln b$$

Expand both sides:
$$2y\ln a - \ln a = x\ln b - y\ln b$$

Collect all terms containing $y$ on the left-hand side:
$$2y\ln a + y\ln b = x\ln b + \ln a$$
$$(2\ln a + \ln b)y = (\ln b)x + \ln a$$

Rearrange into explicit linear form $y = mx + c$:
$$y = \left( \dfrac{\ln b}{2\ln a + \ln b} \right)x + \dfrac{\ln a}{2\ln a + \ln b}$$

Conclude why the graph is a straight line:
Since $a$ and $b$ are constants, the gradient $m = \dfrac{\ln b}{2\ln a + \ln b}$ and $y$-intercept $c = \dfrac{\ln a}{2\ln a + \ln b}$ are constants. The equation matches the standard straight-line form $y = mx + c$, so the graph of $y$ against $x$ is a straight line.

ai_rubric.Linearising Mathematical Models: Uses logs to obtain expression without powers $(2y-1)\ln a = (x-y)\ln b$ (B1). Separates terms and factorises to $(2\ln a+\ln b)y = x\ln b + \ln a$ (B1). Explains equation matches $y=mx+c$ (B1).

hints: Substitute $\ln a = 3\ln b$ into the linear equation from part (a) and cancel common terms.
Express the result in the form $y = px + q$ with exact fractions $p$ and $q$.
walkthrough:
Use the given condition $a = b^3$ to express $\ln a$ in terms of $\ln b$:
$$\ln a = \ln(b^3) = 3\ln b$$

Substitute $\ln a = 3\ln b$ into the rearranged equation $(2\ln a + \ln b)y = (\ln b)x + \ln a$:
$$(2(3\ln b) + \ln b)y = (\ln b)x + 3\ln b$$
$$(6\ln b + \ln b)y = (\ln b)x + 3\ln b$$
$$(7\ln b)y = (\ln b)x + 3\ln b$$

Divide both sides by $\ln b$ (noting $\ln b \neq 0$):
$$7y = x + 3$$

Express in the form $y = px + q$:
$$y = \dfrac{1}{7}x + \dfrac{3}{7}$$

ai_rubric.Linearising Mathematical Models: Uses $a = b^3$ to simplify equation (M1). Obtains $y = \frac{1}{7}x + \frac{3}{7}$ (A1).
